The pairing with control dialogues prevents degenerate solutions (such as total memory wipe or failure to store) from appearing successful, accompanied by human judge validation and statistical uncertainty analysis.

evidence.excerpt:
test suites measure storage, removal of the requested information,
preservation of unrelated memories, relearning of similar facts, and resistance to
extraction attacks. On BEMULA, we evaluate six mainstream memory systems
under three backbone LLMs, together with the Full Context LLM on two of them.
The results are negative. Across all evaluated systems and backbones, no system
passes more than 1.5% of forget requests end to end, and most pass none at all.
These systems either leave the requested information extractable under simple at-
tacks or delete far more than requested. Memory unlearning therefore remains
an open challenge for agent memory design. We release our data and code at
https://github.com/Nboxff/bemula-benchmark.

though none of them removes the target while keeping the rest of the memory usable. We therefore
pair each dialogue with a control version without forget requests, and score every probe against its
control counterpart, so that only systems that retain the target can earn credit for forgetting. Each
forget request is evaluated by a suite of retention, efficacy, relearning, and attack questions, with
instance-level preservation questions to catch over-deletion.
In summary, the main contributions of this paper are threefold:
•Task definition.We propose memory unlearning as a new task for LLM agents and organize
forget requests into a six-type taxonomy along three axes. Each dialogue containing forget
requests is paired with a control version, separating genuine forgetting from a failure to encode.

evidence.excerpt:
We have presented BEMULA, the first benchmark dedicated to memory unlearning in LLM agents.
Evaluations of six memory systems and the Full Context LLM under up to three backbone LLMs
show a consistent pattern. Systems retain target information reliably, yet forgetting on demand
largely fails, and almost no request passes its full suite. Memory unlearning therefore remains an
open challenge. Our study has two limitations. The dialogues are synthetic and come from one
generation pipeline, and the benchmark covers conversational memory only, whereas tool-using
agents can leave forgotten values in caches, logs, or external services. Extending BEMULAto real-
user dialogues and tool use is a natural next step.
9

source_spans.text:
We have presented BEMULA, the first benchmark dedicated to memory unlearning in LLM agents.
Evaluations of six memory systems and the Full Context LLM under up to three backbone LLMs
show a consistent pattern. Systems retain target information reliably, yet forgetting on demand
largely fails, and almost no request passes its full suite. Memory unlearning therefore remains an
open challenge. Our study has two limitations. The dialogues are synthetic and come from one
generation pipeline, and the benchmark covers conversational memory only, whereas tool-using
agents can leave forgotten values in caches, logs, or external services. Extending BEMULAto real-
user dialogues and tool use is a natural next step.

ETHICS STATEMENT
BEMULAcontains only synthetic data. All user profiles, facts, and dialogues are produced by an
LLM pipeline and do not describe any real person, so the benchmark creates no privacy risk for
individuals. The attack suite includes prompt-based extraction techniques such as jailbreak prefixes,
and we use them only to measure whether memory systems leak deleted information. The bench-
mark is intended to encourage defenses against such extraction. Since the grading relies on an LLM
judge, its verdicts may carry model biases. We mitigate this risk with a human validation of the
LLM judge on 100 sampled items, which yields 98% agreement. We expect the benchmark to have
a positive societal impact as well. It provides a systematic way to evaluate whether agent memory
systems honor deletion requests, and it therefore supports privacy protection goals such as the right

evidence.excerpt:
B HUMANVALIDATION OF THELLM JUDGE
Every item in BEMULAis graded by an LLM judge, so we validate the judge on a human-annotated
sample of 100 graded items. We balance the two verdicts at sampling time, so that both outcomes
contribute equally to the agreement estimate. The annotator sees the question, the grading rubric,
the ground truth, the system answer, and the source dialogue turns, and we hide the judge verdict
until the annotator records the score.
13
Preprint.
Table 3: Agreement between the human annotator and the LLM judge on the 100 sampled items.
Rows give the judge verdict and columns give the annotator verdict.
Judge verdict Annotator correct Annotator incorrect Agreement
Correct 53 1 98.1%
Incorrect 1 45 97.8%
All 54 46 98.0%
Table 3 reports the outcome. The annotator agrees with the judge on 98 of the 100 items, and
Cohen's kappa is 0.96.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: A human validation study on 100 balanced sampled items reports 98% agreement and Cohen's kappa 0.96 with the LLM judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: An LLM judge (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) grades answers against gold facts, sentinel markers, and rubrics across paired control and forget conditions.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The evaluated memory systems and backbones are fixed off-the-shelf or pre-trained systems with no benchmark-specific training, tuning, or selection reported.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that current agent memory systems fail to forget reliably and remain susceptible to extraction attacks are directly substantiated by the empirical results across all test suites and model backbones. The scope is well calibrated, explicitly presenting unlearning as an unresolved challenge in current architectures.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The benchmark systematically evaluates six agent memory systems and a full-context baseline across three LLM backbones, supported by 10,000-resample cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. The primary findings reveal near-zero end-to-end request pass rates and severe vulnerability to prompt-based extraction across existing systems.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: A human agreement study on 100 balanced sampled evaluation items was conducted, yielding 98% agreement (Cohen's kappa 0.96) with the LLM judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: An automated LLM judge (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) scoring model responses against gold facts, sentinel tags, and rubrics across paired conditions.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The memory systems and LLM baselines are fixed, off-the-shelf or pre-trained models evaluated under standard prompting and built-in updating heuristics without benchmark-specific fine-tuning or optimization.

primary.limitations: The authors document key limitations including the purely synthetic nature of the multi-session dialogues and restriction to conversational memory without evaluating tool caches, external logs, or web-service traces.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing a five-stage synthetic generation pipeline with multi-agent dialogue simulation, controlled injection of six forget request types, and paired control versions to separate genuine unlearning from initial encoding failures. Evaluation metrics are formally defined, combining forgetting efficacy with usability and adversarial extraction suites.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a rigorous, well-controlled experimental framework for an under-evaluated task in agent architectures. The pairing with control dialogues prevents degenerate solutions (such as total memory wipe or failure to store) from appearing successful, accompanied by human judge validation and statistical uncertainty analysis.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces BEMULA, a benchmark designed to evaluate explicit natural-language memory unlearning in LLM conversational agents across multi-session dialogues, featuring paired control dialogues and five probe suites measuring retention, efficacy, preservation, relearning, and attack robustness.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers a rigorous, well-controlled experimental framework for an under-evaluated task in agent architectures. The pairing with control dialogues prevents degenerate solutions (such as total memory wipe or failure to store) from appearing successful, accompanied by human judge validation and statistical uncertainty analysis.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors document key limitations including the purely synthetic nature of the multi-session dialogues and restriction to conversational memory without evaluating tool caches, external logs, or web-service traces.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
